claims.text: Ab initio calculations can be used to investigate the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
Neutron diffraction can be used to investigate magnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
SQUID magnetometry can be used to investigate magnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
Magnetic behavior in high-entropy oxides can be studied over variable temperatures and magnetic fields.
Configurational entropy correlates with the magnetic and electrical properties of high-entropy perovskite oxides.
The average ionic radius of A-site cations influences the magnetic properties of high-entropy perovskite oxides.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius influence indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius promote the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
Composition can be varied to tune magnetic behavior from macroscopically ordered states toward frustration-driven dynamic spin interactions in high-entropy oxides.
Processing routes can be adjusted to tune high-entropy oxides between macroscopically ordered and frustration-driven dynamic magnetic states.
High-entropy oxides exhibit distinctive magnetic properties.
The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides is influenced by configurational entropy.
The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides is influenced by the average ionic radius of A-site cations.
The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides is influenced by processing routes.
Neutron diffraction and SQUID magnetometry should be applied to HEO samples that vary in composition and processing route.
Failure to observe a correlation among configurational entropy, A-site ionic radius, and magnetic properties would falsify the proposed relationship.
